messages.author: e4c94dbf26a728cc
messages.subject: Issues using corspec
parts:
Hi all,

I am currently using the corspec function and have trouble with it, I
need help!
I have already written a script to prepare my soundfiles and do the
frequency spectra using meanspec. This involved cutting the sound
files to get the signal only and get rid of the silence on each side
of the signal, doing a band-pass filter to keep frequencies from 500
to 10000Hz only, and calculating the mean spectrum of 10 different
calls from one individual.
So there was some matrix modifications involved, and I saved the data
as a two-columns text file, using
write.table(specMean, "SpecM1_2m", row.names=FALSE)

Then I tried comparing two spectra using corspec, and got this error
message:
Erreur dans cor(x = spec1, y = c(spec2[(i + 1):n2], rep(0, i)), method
= method) :
'y' must be numeric

I checked my specs, and found that the column names had been changed
in the process to "V1" and "V2" so I changed them back to "x" and "y",
but it still doesn't work.

My "spec" variable looks like this:
> head(spec1)
x y
1 0.5167969 0.03273822
2 0.5598633 0.09213714
3 0.6029297 0.09989777
4 0.6459961 0.07955930
5 0.6890625 0.08882194
6 0.7321289 0.08160801

Do you have an idea to get it work?

Also, I suggest that the option of choosing a F-min and F-max to band
pass the sound could be added directly to the corspec function. What
do you think?

Thank you for your help.

messages.author: 44c03a0165efd08f
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Issues using corspec
parts:
Hi,

I would double check that the values in your matrices/data.frames are
numeric. Sometimes when you load in data files, the values are imported
as text rather than numbers.

To check:

> class(spec1$x)

if you get "numeric", then there is a different problem. However, if you
get "character" then the problem is that R views your values as text.

To change it, you could run

> spec1$x = as.numeric(spec1$x)
> spec1$y = as.numeric(spec1$y)

(There is probably a more elegant way of doing this, but this is the
quick and dirty way).

Let me know if this helps!

Steffi

parts:
Ok, so the reason why corspec didn't recognised my data was that I
saved it as a data.frame (using write.table). So we need to convert
the data to a matrix :

spec1 <- as.matrix(spec1)
spec2 <- as.matrix(spec2)

Then corspec works:
corspec(spec1,spec2)

Thank you Jerome!
